projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I expect it will be desirable before thou leaves the billet to hear from thy grandaughter Rebecca, although as thou might have observed the carriage to be pretty full as rode pretty comfortable down to Thomas Walmsleys in about 3 hours, and after refreshing ourselves Recbecca & myself got home about 5 o’clock. She appeared better satisfied than I could have expected. We were at Meeting yesterday, (where James Simpson was much favored in public testimony) She also appears to take a discretionary pleasure in little Priscilla Kirk’s company, which she has had the opportunity of for several house together. She rode over to T. Walmsely’s with James Simpson & myself this afternoon, & returned cheerfully. I discover no other but she is reconciled to her new home, which I was doubtful of before trial, feeling my inability to attract the attention & affection of the child in such a manner as I thought would be expedient–which occasioned one to utter fewer words on the occasion than I should otherwise have done, but inasmuch as her father & thou has entrusted her with me I feel an increasing desire to extend a steady tender care over her every way as far as I may be enabled through immediate and instrumental help. I feel of myself I am not able to do any good thing, therefore crave the prayers of my Friends. Also that I may he engaged for myself, I don’t feel qualified to enlarge, but according to my measure having had sympathetically to feel for thee, as it has been my portion to partake of many bitter cups similar to thine of latter time.

closer.salute: in much love I conclude and bid thee affectionately farewell-
